newsitem.title: USA: Illinois group maps out electric deregulation plan.
newsitem.headline: Illinois group maps out electric deregulation plan.

text.p: A coalition of electric utilities and business groups in Illinois unveiled on Tuesday draft legislation aimed at deregulating the electricity industry within the state.

The plan by the Illinois Coalition for Responsible Electricity Choice called for opening the door to limited competition for a "significant number of Illinois residential, commercial and industrial electricity customers" starting in 1998 and completing the deregulation process statewide in 2005. The plan would also cap electricity rates at their current levels until 2000.
Electricity customers who choose to leave their current supplier would pay a transition charge to compensate utilities for prior mandated investments.

Local news reports have raised the possibility of state bond sales backed by the charges to raise the money to pay back the utilities. Coalition representatives were not scheduled to discuss the plan until a telephone conference call scheduled for 1430 CST/2030 GMT Tuesday.

According to a news release from the coalition, the draft legislation would reform regulation of utilities to accomodate a competitive environment, require utilities to rebate to customers half of any profits exceeding specified levels during the transition period and assign oversight responsibility for reliability and safety issues to the Illinois Commerce Commission.
The group said the draft bill addresses so-called guiding principles suggested by the Illinois General Assembly's Joint Committee on Electric Utility Regulatory Reform.

But legislators are unlikely to take up any deregulation plan during its fall veto session, which began Tuesday, according to Patty Schuh, spokeswoman for Senate President James "Pate" Philip, R-Wood Dale.
In fact, a report from the legislative joint committee has yet to be drafted, according to a legislative source.

The coalition consists of Unicom Corp's Commonwealth Edison, CIPSCO Inc's Central Illinois Public Service Co , Illinois Industrial Electricity Consumers, Chemical Industries Council of Illinois, Illinois Manufacturers' Association, Illinois Power Co, Illinois Retail Merchants Association, MidAmerican Energy Co and Union Electric Co.
